title: Atoms
seo_title: Atoms Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)
standard_text: Alpha-particle scattering experiment; Rutherford's model of atom; Bohr model of hydrogen atom, expression for radius of nth possible orbit, velocity and energy of electron in nth orbit, hydrogen line spectra (qualitative treatment only).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 12 Atoms: α-particle scattering, Rutherford's model, Bohr's model, orbit radii and energies, and the hydrogen spectrum. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A jump between levels gives one spectral line.
body_html:
How to think about it

In the Geiger–Marsden experiment most α-particles went straight through gold foil, but a few bounced back, showing a tiny, massive, positive nucleus. Rutherford's model could not explain why atoms are stable or why spectra have lines.

Bohr's model allows only orbits with angular momentum nh/2π. For hydrogen rn = 0.53 n² Å and En = −13.6/n² eV. When an electron falls between levels it emits a photon of energy equal to the difference; the Lyman series ends on n = 1, Balmer (visible) on n = 2 and Paschen on n = 3.

Example

H, n = 2. Energy?

−13.6 ÷ 4

Answer: −3.4 eV

Example

n = 3 → 2 photon?

1.89 eV

Answer: 656 nm

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the minus sign of energy.
  • Saying r ∝ n.
  • Naming the series by the upper level.
